sections.heading: Locations
mechanicsSummary: Cities and havens are both locations.
A card that names a city cannot be used on a haven, and a card that names a haven cannot be used on a city.
A location with an anchor symbol is a port.

sections.heading: Havens
mechanicsSummary: Havens are the white locations that have an anchor.
At the start of the campaign the group names the three havens on the board.

sections.heading: Population
mechanicsSummary: Every location has a population from 0 through 8.
Population is how many supply cubes a Produce Supplies card places there.
Status bands: Recovering 8–6, Surviving 5–3, Struggling 2, Falling 1, Forsaken 0.

sections.heading: Supply Lines
mechanicsSummary: No supply lines exist at the start.
Later, supply lines connect cities across land. Two cities joined by a supply line are adjacent.

sections.heading: Sea Lanes & Sea Routes
mechanicsSummary: Sea lanes connect locations across the ocean. Two locations joined by a sea lane are adjacent.
A sea route is a chain of connected sea lanes.

sections.heading: The Grid
mechanicsSummary: Most of the board starts blank.
The grid is every location that can be traced back to the starting havens along supply lines and/or sea lanes.

sections.heading: Expanding the Grid
mechanicsSummary: World-map stickers are added to the board when opened, lined up on the latitude and longitude lines.

sections.heading: Objectives Section
mechanicsSummary: One corner of the board holds objective cards.
January starts with two objectives.
Later months add and remove objectives. Overflow objectives sit beside the board.

sections.heading: Game End Area
mechanicsSummary: Some instructions place cards in the Game End area during the game.
At the end of the game, take every card from that area and follow it.

sections.heading: Incident Track
mechanicsSummary: Counts how many times a plague cube has been placed on a location.
Removing plague cubes does not move the Incident marker backward.
When the marker reaches the end of the track, the players lose immediately.

sections.heading: Supply Cube Stockpile
mechanicsSummary: The stockpile is the shared pool of supply cubes in play.
Unless a card or effect says otherwise, supply cubes are taken from the stockpile and returned to it.
When an effect tells a player to spend supply cubes, those cubes come off that player's Character card and go back to the stockpile.
At game end, every supply cube still in the stockpile goes to the reserve. Stockpile contents do not carry into the next game.
